purpose: Regulator-authored named product cases in which the clinical molecule lacks an ordinary pharmacologically relevant experimental animal species and a surrogate molecule/model was nevertheless used for substantive animal toxicology. This dataset is kept separate from direct relevant-species toxicology and from human-relevant omission cases.

cases.clinical_product_species_relevance: Eculizumab is specific for human C5 and no other tested species exhibited a pharmacologically active response.
cases.surrogate_strategy: Toxicity testing used BB5.1, a surrogate murine anti-mouse C5 antibody, including 4-week and 26-week repeat-dose studies and reproductive/developmental studies in mice; a human-C5-reconstituted mouse model was used for selected PK/PD questions.
cases.why_it_matters: Provides an early same-target precursor to Ultomiris showing the surrogate-C5 strategy used when the clinical antibody lacked a relevant animal species.

cases.modality: CD19 x CD3 bispecific T-cell engager
cases.clinical_product_species_relevance: Blinatumomab binds human and chimpanzee B/T cells but does not bind lymphocytes of other animal species.
cases.surrogate_strategy: Rat anti-mouse antibodies against murine CD19 and CD3 were engineered into a surrogate molecule for a comprehensive general and specialized mouse toxicology program; limited short-duration chimpanzee infusions were also performed.
cases.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that species non-relevance can lead to surrogate-animal substitution rather than omission of conventional toxicology.

cases.clinical_product_species_relevance: Ravulizumab does not bind non-human C5; Health Canada states there are no animal species with a pharmacologically active response to the clinical molecule.
cases.surrogate_strategy: A surrogate antibody against murine C5 was used for a 26-week repeat-dose toxicity study and reproductive studies in mice.
cases.why_it_matters: Shows a mature biologics program using surrogate toxicology when the clinical antibody lacks a pharmacologically active animal species.

cases.clinical_product_species_relevance: Teplizumab cross-reactivity is limited to humans, chimpanzees, gorillas and other species that are not established experimental species.
cases.surrogate_strategy: Health Canada reviewed a package with one chimpanzee study plus repeat-dose and reproductive/developmental toxicology using a surrogate anti-mouse CD3 antibody; in-vitro binding studies were used to establish surrogate relevance.
cases.why_it_matters: A 2025 authorization demonstrates that surrogate toxicology remains a contemporary regulatory strategy and is not merely an older historical practice.

policy_contrast.policy: For drug substances that are not pharmacologically active in animals, MHRA states that it does not support testing in animals, including with surrogate molecules; non-animal-based methods can suffice for efficacy and safety expectations for this group.
policy_contrast.interpretation: This is a regulator-policy contrast, not proof that another regulator would reject a Health Canada-style surrogate package. It establishes that current regulatory approaches to the same species-nonrelevance problem are not fully converged.
